method: The authors solve the nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics analytically in a synthetic lattice with exactly solvable interacting dynamics, deriving a wave-packet-dependent band structure and temporal refractive response.
result: They uncover amplitude-dependent temporal reflection/refraction, nonlinear temporal birefringence, and gradient-induced Bloch oscillations that suppress diffusion and enable coherent periodic transport.
conclusion: The work provides a tractable framework for nonlinear wave manipulation in synthetic lattices, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Linear And Nonlinear Optical Torque In Multi-level Atomic Systems Driven By Counter-rotating Orbital Angular Momentum Fields
authors: Dharma P. Permana, Ma\v{z}ena Mackoit Sinkevi\v{c}ien\.e, Via\v{c}eslav Kudria\v{s}ov, Julius Ruseckas, Gediminas Juzeli\"unas, Hamid R. Hamedi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the generation of optical torque in coherently prepared multi-level atomic media driven by a vector vortex beam composed of two counter-rotating components carrying opposite orbital angular momenta, [MATH] and [MATH]. We consider a three-level [MATH] configuration and a four-level tripod configuration. Using a perturbative steady-state solution of the optical Bloch equations, we obtain analytical expressions for both linear and nonlinear contributions to the optical torque. The results show that the torque is strongly controlled by atomic coherence, including the initial population imbalance and the relative phase between the vortex components. Nonvanishing torque can arise even when the two components have equal amplitudes, due to coherence-induced asymmetry in the atomic response. In the tripod configuration, the presence of a strong control field leads to electromagnetically induced transparency, which suppresses the torque near resonance and shifts the dominant response to finite detunings. These results establish a route for controlling light-induced rotational dynamics in atomic media using vector vortex fields, with potential applications in coherent optical manipulation and angular-momentum-based control in quantum systems.
tldr: This paper studies optical torque generation in multi-level atomic systems using counter-rotating orbital angular momentum fields, focusing on coherence control and nonlinear effects.
motivation: To understand and control light-induced rotational dynamics in atomic media, with potential applications in coherent optical manipulation.
method: Perturbative steady-state solution of optical Bloch equations for three-level Λ and four-level tripod configurations driven by a vector vortex beam.
result: Optical torque is strongly controlled by atomic coherence; nonvanishing torque can arise even with equal amplitudes due to coherence-induced asymmetry; in tripod configuration, EIT suppresses torque near resonance.
conclusion: The results establish a route for controlling rotational dynamics using vector vortex fields, relevant to angular-momentum-based control in quantum systems.

title: The Beg Model At The Fad Triple Point On The Square Lattice
authors: Estev\~ao F. Borel, Aldo Procacci, R\'emy Sanchis, Benedetto Scoppola
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we prove that the two-dimensional Blume-Emery-Griffiths model at the triple point Ferromagnetic-Antiquadrupolar-Disordered (FAD) has a unique Gibbs measure at any temperature, thereby establishing the absence of phase transitions. The FAD point lies at the intersection of lines separating three regions of the phase diagram, and it is a singular point where the model exhibits infinitely many ground states. Our proof is based on a random-cluster type representation with configuration-dependent cluster weights and a coupling with Bernoulli site percolation with parameter [MATH].
tldr: This paper proves the absence of phase transitions for the Blume-Emery-Griffiths model at the FAD triple point on the square lattice.
motivation: The FAD triple point is a singular point with infinitely many ground states, and understanding its phase behavior is a challenging problem in statistical mechanics.
method: The proof uses a random-cluster type representation with configuration-dependent cluster weights and a coupling with Bernoulli site percolation.
result: It is shown that the model has a unique Gibbs measure at any temperature at the FAD triple point.
conclusion: The result establishes the absence of phase transitions at this singular point, contributing to the rigorous understanding of the BEG model phase diagram.

title: Metric Congruence In Finite-Dimensional Non-Hermitian Quantum Mechanics
authors: Reboiro Marta Ramirez Romina
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study metric representations in finite-dimensional non-Hermitian quantum mechanics. The main purpose of this work is to emphasize that the physical description of a non-Hermitian system may be formulated in different, but isomorphic, Hilbert spaces. In particular, within the Krein-space formalism, we show that the vector space endowed with an indefinite Krein metric can be explicitly related to the standard Hilbert space through a suitable isomorphism. This observation is essential for a consistent description of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. Physical states, metrics, and operators must be transported through the corresponding Hilbert-space isomorphism. In this way, equivalent representations of the same system can be used without changing the physical content of the theory. We illustrate these theoretical aspects by studying a two-level non-Hermitian spin model. We use the Robertson uncertainty relation as a consistency test. Apparent violations can arise when operators and states are kept fixed while the metric is changed, and therefore reflect a mismatch of representations rather than a failure of the uncertainty principle.
tldr: This paper studies metric representations in finite-dimensional non-Hermitian quantum mechanics, emphasizing the equivalence of different Hilbert-space formulations.
motivation: To clarify that non-Hermitian systems can be described in different but isomorphic Hilbert spaces, and to show that apparent violations of uncertainty relations arise from representation mismatches.
method: Uses Krein-space formalism to relate indefinite metric spaces to standard Hilbert spaces via isomorphisms, and tests consistency with Robertson uncertainty relation on a two-level non-Hermitian spin model.
result: Demonstrates that changing the metric while keeping operators and states fixed can lead to apparent violations of the uncertainty principle, which are resolved by properly transporting states and operators through the isomorphism.
conclusion: A consistent description of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians requires transporting physical states, metrics, and operators through the Hilbert-space isomorphism to avoid representation mismatches.

title: Unit-Circle Moment Closure
authors: Yao Wang Yu Su
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moment closure is a central problem in reduced descriptions of stochastic, kinetic, and quantum dynamics, where equations for low-order observables are coupled to an unresolved hierarchy of higher-order moments. Existing closures usually impose a prescribed form on the distribution or directly truncate the hierarchy, which can become inaccurate or unstable for strongly non-Gaussian states. Here we introduce unit-circle moment closure, which recasts the problem as analytic continuation. Raw moments are mapped to bounded unit-circle moments, whose unresolved tail is reconstructed by a Takagi-Prony procedure from the effective pole structure of a mapped generating function. The resulting continuation yields stable higher-order moments without assuming a fixed distributional ansatz. Illustrative static and dynamical examples demonstrate accurate reconstruction of non-Gaussian distributions and stable evolution of moment hierarchies. Our approach provides a general perspective for moment closure based on analytic structure rather than direct truncation.
tldr: Introduces a moment closure method based on analytic continuation using unit-circle moments and Takagi-Prony reconstruction.
motivation: Existing moment closure methods for stochastic, kinetic, and quantum dynamics are inaccurate or unstable for strongly non-Gaussian states.
method: Maps raw moments to bounded unit-circle moments and reconstructs the unresolved tail via Takagi-Prony procedure from the pole structure of a mapped generating function.
result: Demonstrates accurate reconstruction of non-Gaussian distributions and stable evolution of moment hierarchies in static and dynamical examples.
conclusion: Provides a general perspective for moment closure based on analytic structure rather than direct truncation.

title: A High-Performance Pauli-Algebra Framework For Large-Scale Quantum Simulations
authors: Xiaopeng Li, Zhijie Sun, Yi Fan, Jie Liu, Zhenyu Li, Jinlong Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient manipulation of Pauli-algebraic objects is a key bottleneck in the classical emulation and benchmarking of quantum algorithms for chemistry and many-body physics. This bottleneck appears in Hamiltonian construction, variational ansatz preparation, expectation-value and gradient evaluation, and real-time propagation, all of which require repeated Pauli-algebra operations. Here, we present a high-performance Pauli-algebra framework tailored to quantum many-body and quantum-chemical simulations. The framework combines compact binary symplectic encoding, canonical coefficient reduction, and grouped sparse operator representations that exploit shared bit-flip patterns among Pauli strings. The resulting Julia/C implementation accelerates Pauli multiplication, Hamiltonian construction, and operator--state multiplication in sparse and symmetry-adapted many-electron spaces. Benchmarks demonstrate efficient Hamiltonian construction, large-active-space VQE and ADAPT-VQE calculations, and real-time variational dynamics on modern multicore CPU and GPU architectures. These results show that structure-aware Pauli-algebra engines provide a scalable classical backend for developing and benchmarking quantum algorithms in quantum chemistry and many-body simulation.
tldr: A high-performance Pauli-algebra framework for classical simulation of quantum algorithms in chemistry and many-body physics.
motivation: Efficient manipulation of Pauli-algebraic objects is a bottleneck in classical emulation and benchmarking of quantum algorithms.
method: Combines compact binary symplectic encoding, canonical coefficient reduction, and grouped sparse operator representations in a Julia/C implementation.
result: Benchmarks show efficient Hamiltonian construction, VQE and ADAPT-VQE calculations, and real-time variational dynamics on multicore CPU and GPU architectures.
conclusion: Structure-aware Pauli-algebra engines provide a scalable classical backend for developing and benchmarking quantum algorithms.

title: Cohomological Beta Function
authors: Oleksandr Gamayun, Maxim Gritskov, Andrey Losev
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a cohomological approach to computing the conformal anomaly. Using the example of current-current deformations of two-dimensional conformal field theories, we reproduce the well-known Cardy formula for the leading contribution to the perturbative beta function as the coefficient of the cocycle that realizes the obstruction to deforming the Virasoro module structure on the state space. In addition to offering a novel conceptual perspective on the conformal anomaly, the proposed approach is anticipated to provide an efficient tool for computing higher-order coefficients of perturbative beta functions.
tldr: This paper proposes a cohomological approach to compute the conformal anomaly in two-dimensional conformal field theories, using current-current deformations to reproduce the Cardy formula for the perturbative beta function.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a novel conceptual perspective on the conformal anomaly and develop an efficient tool for computing higher-order coefficients of perturbative beta functions.
method: They use cohomological methods to compute the obstruction to deforming the Virasoro module structure on the state space, which yields the beta function as a cocycle coefficient.
result: The approach reproduces the well-known Cardy formula for the leading contribution to the perturbative beta function.
conclusion: The cohomological approach offers a new perspective on the conformal anomaly and is anticipated to be efficient for higher-order calculations.

title: Continuous Modal Spectrum In Nonreciprocal Cavities
authors: Filipa R. Prud\^encio, David E. Fernandes, M\'ario G. Silveirinha
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonreciprocal systems enable asymmetric energy transport and suppress backscattering, giving rise to unconventional wave phenomena. Here, we show that nonreciprocal cavities based on unidirectional waveguides exhibit a continuous modal spectrum, in contrast to conventional cavities with discrete eigenmodes. Using a ferrite-loaded microwave cavity as an example, we demonstrate that enforcing unidirectionality, by tailoring the waveguide geometry, drives a transition from discrete to continuous spectra, accompanied by strong spatial localization of electromagnetic fields. Our results reveal that dissipation alone fails to regularize these singular responses, highlighting the need for additional mechanisms to control localization in nonreciprocal systems.
tldr: This paper studies continuous modal spectra in nonreciprocal cavities using ferrite-loaded microwave waveguides.
motivation: To understand the transition from discrete to continuous spectra in nonreciprocal cavities and the role of dissipation.
method: The authors analyze a ferrite-loaded microwave cavity with unidirectional waveguide geometry, using theoretical modeling and numerical simulations.
result: They show that enforcing unidirectionality leads to a continuous modal spectrum with strong spatial localization, and dissipation alone cannot regularize the singular response.
conclusion: Additional mechanisms are needed to control localization in nonreciprocal systems.

title: On The Fischer-Musz\'ely Equation For The Positive Cones Of $C^*$-algebras
authors: Jyamira Oppekepenguin Daisuke Hirota
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Fischer-Musz\'ely functional equation for the positive semidefinite and the positive definite cones of unital [MATH]-algebras. We show that any bijection between the positive semidefinite cones satisfying the Fischer-Musz\'ely equality extends to a Jordan [MATH]-isomorphism followed by multiplication on both sides by a positive element. As a corollary, we obtain a similar result for the positive definite cones of unital [MATH]-algebras.
tldr: The paper studies the Fischer-Muszély functional equation on positive cones of C*-algebras, establishing that bijections satisfying the equation extend to Jordan *-isomorphisms.
motivation: To characterize the structure-preserving maps on positive cones of C*-algebras via a functional equation, which is a purely mathematical problem.
method: The authors analyze bijections on positive semidefinite and positive definite cones that satisfy the Fischer-Muszély equality, and use algebraic techniques to show they extend to Jordan *-isomorphisms.
result: Any bijection between positive semidefinite cones satisfying the Fischer-Muszély equality extends to a Jordan *-isomorphism followed by multiplication by a positive element; a similar result holds for positive definite cones.
conclusion: The Fischer-Muszély equation provides a characterization of Jordan *-isomorphisms on positive cones of unital C*-algebras.

title: Abundance Of Minimal Measures Via Entropy And Multifractal Analysis
authors: Xiaobo Hou, Wanshan Lin, Xueting Tian, Yi Yuan, Xutong Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the distribution and abundance of minimal measures (measures supported on minimal sets) in various dynamical systems, extending the well-known density results for general ergodic measures. We introduce the conditional minimal-intermediate-entropy property, which asserts that for any given entropy [MATH] and potential integral [MATH], the set of ergodic minimal measures satisfying [MATH] and [MATH] is dense in the set of invariant measures satisfying these conditions. We establish that the conditional minimal-intermediate-entropy property holds for three broad classes of systems: topologically expanding maps (including topologically Anosov systems), transitive countable Markov shifts, and symbolic systems with non-uniform structure. Our proofs rely on a constructive multi-horseshoe technique adapted to handle challenges of non-compactness and non-uniformity.
tldr: This paper studies the abundance of minimal measures in dynamical systems using entropy and multifractal analysis.
motivation: To understand the distribution and density of minimal measures in various dynamical systems, extending known results for ergodic measures.
method: Introduces the conditional minimal-intermediate-entropy property and uses a constructive multi-horseshoe technique to handle non-compactness and non-uniformity.
result: Establishes the property for topologically expanding maps, transitive countable Markov shifts, and symbolic systems with non-uniform structure.
conclusion: Minimal measures are abundant in these systems, providing a deeper understanding of their structure.

title: Salami Slicing Trellis For Synchronization Errors In Dna Coding
authors: Tsung-Han Wu, Joseph Swernofsky, Hsin-Po Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On top of substitution errors, DNA storage channels suffer from both insertions and deletions at the same time. It is therefore important to develop error-correcting codes with efficient encoders and decoders that can combat all three types of noise. This paper introduces the salami-slicing trellis, a decision-feedback trellis that computes bitwise posterior probabilities along each strand and is coupled with polar codes across strands. The decoder alternates between advancing the trellises by one position and polar-decoding the resulting cross-strand slice, feeding the decoded bits back to the trellises for the next position. Simulations suggest that the resulting coding scheme approaches the conjectured capacity of the substitution-insertion-deletion channel.
tldr: This paper presents a coding scheme for DNA storage channels that corrects substitution, insertion, and deletion errors using a salami-slicing trellis and polar codes.
motivation: DNA storage channels suffer from simultaneous insertions and deletions, making it necessary to develop error-correcting codes that handle all three types of noise efficiently.
method: The authors introduce a salami-slicing trellis that computes bitwise posterior probabilities along each strand, coupled with polar codes across strands. The decoder alternates between advancing the trellis and polar-decoding cross-strand slices.
result: Simulations show the coding scheme approaches the conjectured capacity of the substitution-insertion-deletion channel.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical approach to error correction in DNA storage, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Lumping Of Reaction Networks: Generic And Critical Parameters
authors: Justin Eilertsen, Valery G. Romanovski, Santiago Schnell, Sebastian Walcher
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate linear lumping for parameter-dependent mass action reaction networks, distinguishing between generic and critical parameter regimes. For generic parameters -- those ranging in some non-empty open subset of parameter space -- we prove that exact linear lumping yields only "obvious" reductions: elimination of non-reactant species or projections along stoichiometric first integrals. This characterization extends to reaction networks with product-form kinetics, including Michaelis-Menten and Hill-type rate laws. For mass action systems we proceed to develop an algorithmic approach to identify critical parameter sets -- algebraic subvarieties in parameter space where non-trivial lumpings become available. This procedure reduces the determination of lumping maps to a system of finitely many polynomial equations. It also applies to constrained lumping scenarios (which are frequently motivated by chemical considerations). We then review and extend results about proper lumpings. Finally, we discuss lumpings of a self-replicator system, and of a two-pathway enzyme mechanism, to document the viability of our methods in relevant scenarios. Our results clarify the relationship between structural (parameter-independent) and fine-tuned (parameter-dependent) reductions, with implications for approximate lumping when system parameters lie near critical values.
tldr: This paper studies linear lumping of parameter-dependent mass action reaction networks, distinguishing generic and critical parameter regimes.
motivation: To understand when non-trivial reductions of reaction networks are possible, which has implications for model simplification and approximate lumping near critical parameters.
method: The authors prove that for generic parameters only obvious reductions exist, and develop an algorithmic approach using polynomial equations to identify critical parameter sets where non-trivial lumpings occur.
result: Generic parameters yield only trivial reductions; non-trivial lumpings are confined to algebraic subvarieties of parameter space. The method is demonstrated on a self-replicator system and a two-pathway enzyme mechanism.
conclusion: The work clarifies the relationship between structural and fine-tuned reductions, and provides tools for identifying parameter-dependent lumpings.

title: Distributed Recursive Binary Identification Under Tampering And Non-persistent Excitation
authors: Ji-Feng Zhang Jian Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider distributed parameter estimation with binary observations under measurement-side tampering: each node observes a thresholded output whose label may be flipped and exchanges information over a communication graph. We develop a distributed recursive projection algorithm based on the diffusion strategy. Without imposing independence, stationarity, or Gaussian assumptions, we establish almost sure upper bounds of both the accumulated regrets of the adaptive predictor and the distributed estimation error. Under a mild cooperative excitation condition, all nodes' estimate are consistent, even when each node is individually non-exciting. Simulations on a jointly exciting network corroborate the theory and show that the proposed algorithm converges, whereas non-cooperative and tampering-unaware baselines do not.
tldr: This paper proposes a distributed recursive projection algorithm for parameter estimation with binary observations under measurement-side tampering, without requiring independence or stationarity assumptions.
motivation: Distributed parameter estimation with binary observations is challenging when measurements are tampered with and individual nodes lack persistent excitation.
method: A distributed recursive projection algorithm based on the diffusion strategy is developed, and almost sure upper bounds on accumulated regrets and estimation error are established under a cooperative excitation condition.
result: The algorithm converges and all nodes' estimates are consistent under mild cooperative excitation, even when each node is individually non-exciting.
conclusion: The proposed method outperforms non-cooperative and tampering-unaware baselines, as demonstrated by simulations on a jointly exciting network.

title: Sharp $O(1/k)$ Convergence Rate For The Sinkhorn Algorithm Via A Local Analysis
authors: Guillaume Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the Sinkhorn algorithm converges at the rate of [MATH] in [MATH]-norm marginal error and in joint relative entropy, which is known to be sharp in the asymptotically scalable case. The proof is based on examining the bipartite graph associated to the entropy-regularized optimal transport problem, and treating differently the edges that are assigned a positive mass in the optimal transport plan vs. those that are not. This yields a local convergence bound with the sharp rate, which is bootstrapped into a global bound using the author's previous result in arXiv:2604.26265 where we showed an almost-sharp rate up to a logarithmic factor.
tldr: This paper proves a sharp O(1/k) convergence rate for the Sinkhorn algorithm in optimal transport, using a local analysis of the bipartite graph.
motivation: The Sinkhorn algorithm is widely used for entropy-regularized optimal transport, but its exact convergence rate was not fully understood; previous work had only an almost-sharp rate up to a logarithmic factor.
method: The proof examines the bipartite graph associated with the optimal transport problem, treating edges with positive mass in the optimal plan differently from those without, leading to a local convergence bound that is then bootstrapped to a global bound using a previous result.
result: The Sinkhorn algorithm converges at rate O(1/k) in marginal error and joint relative entropy, which is sharp in the asymptotically scalable case.
conclusion: This resolves the convergence rate of the Sinkhorn algorithm, confirming optimality and providing a complete theoretical understanding.

title: Residual-Guided Dictionary Learning For Spectrally Accurate Koopman Approximation
authors: Matthew J. Colbrook George Coote
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Koopman theory promises linear structure in nonlinear dynamics, but numerical Koopman spectra are easy to compute and hard to trust. A finite EDMD matrix always has eigenvalues; the problem is that many of them may have nothing to do with the infinite-dimensional operator. In this paper we make spectral reliability the objective of dictionary learning. We train neural-network dictionaries not merely to predict the next snapshot, but to minimize Residual Dynamic Mode Decomposition residuals: operator-level a posteriori errors that test whether computed eigenvalues and modes are genuine Koopman spectral objects. To keep the learned observables from collapsing into an unstable coordinate system, the loss also penalizes the condition number of the lifted data matrix. Thus the method couples two requirements that should not be separated: small Koopman residuals and a well-conditioned representation. The result is a learned dictionary that is expressive, numerically stable, and spectrally disciplined. Across conservative and dissipative benchmark systems, the method sharply reduces spectral pollution, improves residual pseudospectral inclusion, and lowers forecast error relative to standard fixed dictionaries. On sea-surface temperature data, it gives cleaner Koopman diagnostics and substantially better one-step forecasts from noisy observations with no governing equations. The message is simple: neural Koopman learning should be judged not by prediction alone, but by whether its spectral claims can be certified. Residuals provide the certificate; conditioning makes it computable.
tldr: This paper proposes a residual-guided dictionary learning method for computing reliable Koopman spectra from data.
motivation: Standard EDMD yields spurious eigenvalues that do not correspond to the true Koopman operator, making spectral analysis unreliable.
method: Neural-network dictionaries are trained to minimize residual dynamic mode decomposition errors and penalize the condition number of the lifted data matrix.
result: The method reduces spectral pollution, improves residual pseudospectral inclusion, and lowers forecast error on benchmark systems and sea-surface temperature data.
conclusion: Neural Koopman learning should be certified by residuals rather than prediction accuracy alone.

title: Tool Use Enables Undetectable Steganography In Multi-Agent Llm Systems
authors: Jimmy Laurence Rippin, Simon C. Marshall, David Demitri Africa, Christian Schroeder de Witt
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Increasingly autonomous agentic AI systems pose novel multi-agent risks, such as secret collusion via covert communication channels. The natural defence to these collusion attempts is to monitor plain-text communication, but the efficacy of monitors has been called into doubt by increasingly sophisticated model steganography; indeed, some theoretical schemes have been proposed that are information-theoretically or computationally indistinguishable from good-faith plain-text communication. In this paper, we demonstrate that the complexity of these schemes is no longer a safety barrier, as agentic coding models can already produce undetectable stegosystems when given realistic tool usage, such as code execution or accessing research papers through web searches. Agents also adapt when key ingredients are missing, for example, by adding model-sampling components or implementing related keyed coding schemes. We then frame tacit steganographic coordination between agents as a Schelling-point problem and introduce coordination metrics for estimating when two agents are likely to select compatible schemes without explicit prior agreement. Our results suggest a shift in the threat model for covert communication between AI agents, where the main barrier is no longer whether frontier agents can understand and implement sophisticated stegosystems, but coordination: whether independently acting agents can converge on compatible schemes, keys, and parameters. We find substantial convergence on broad scheme families but limited strict one-shot coordination, suggesting that shared artefacts, repeated interaction, and tool-mediated search are the settings where covert communication risks are most acute. Overall, our findings provide empirical grounding for the recent strategic confinement hypothesis, which assumes that capable agents can construct covert channels that survive monitoring.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that AI agents can use tools like code execution to create undetectable steganographic channels, posing risks of secret collusion.
motivation: As AI agents become more autonomous, they may collude via covert communication, evading monitors. The paper investigates whether current models can implement sophisticated steganography using available tools.
method: The authors test frontier LLMs with tool access (code execution, web search) to generate steganographic schemes, and analyze coordination between agents using Schelling-point metrics.
result: Agents can produce undetectable stegosystems when given tools, and show convergence on broad scheme families but limited one-shot coordination.
conclusion: The main barrier to covert communication is coordination, not capability; shared artifacts and repeated interaction heighten risks, supporting the strategic confinement hypothesis.

title: Decomposing Memorization Reduction In Privacy-Preserving Fine-Tuning Of SLMs For CSIRTs
authors: Diego Kreutz Cristhian Kapelinski
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: CSIRTs increasingly fine tune language models on vulnerability scan records, but these records expose internal network topology and create privacy risks under regulations such as GDPR and LGPD. We present the first empirical study of how DP SGD and HMAC pseudonymization interact when fine tuning small language models with 1B to 3B parameters on structured CSIRT data. We evaluate 96 LoRA adapters across four SLMs and four training regimes, including raw fine tuning, QLoRA with large batch training, and DP SGD with epsilon equal to 2 and 8. We also audit memorization using 20 planted canaries, four extraction attacks, and a dual attack targeting HMAC pseudonymized identifiers. Our results show three main findings. First, matched update controls reproduce the observed reduction in memorization by reducing the number of optimizer updates alone, accounting for 66 percent to 132 percent of the measured effect, with a mean of 100 percent across three seeds and four models. In this setting, DP SGD provides the formal privacy guarantee but does not produce additional measurable reductions in memorization. Second, HMAC pseudonymization removes the original identifiers from the exposure surface, reducing exposure by 40 percent to 61 percent, while pseudonymized identifiers remain close to the expected random baseline and do not become a secondary memorization target. Third, F1 scores remain between 0.19 and 0.28 across all 96 adapters using four shot prompting, indicating that, under the evaluated training budget, 1B to 3B SLMs do not achieve operationally useful performance.
tldr: This paper studies memorization reduction in privacy-preserving fine-tuning of small language models for CSIRTs using DP-SGD and HMAC pseudonymization.
motivation: CSIRTs fine-tune language models on vulnerability scan records that expose internal network topology, creating privacy risks under GDPR and LGPD.
method: The authors evaluate 96 LoRA adapters across four SLMs (1B-3B parameters) and four training regimes, including DP-SGD with epsilon=2 and 8, and HMAC pseudonymization, auditing memorization with planted canaries and extraction attacks.
result: Matched update controls account for 66%-132% of memorization reduction (mean 100%), DP-SGD provides formal guarantees but no additional measurable reduction, and HMAC pseudonymization reduces exposure by 40%-61%.
conclusion: Under the evaluated training budget, 1B-3B SLMs do not achieve operationally useful performance (F1 0.19-0.28), and DP-SGD's effect on memorization is fully explained by reduced optimizer updates.

title: Capability Gates Are Not Authorization: Confused-Deputy Failures In Llm Agent Frameworks
authors: David Mellafe Zuvic
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using LLM agents increasingly read untrusted content while holding side-effecting tools such as payments, email, CRM, and infrastructure APIs, yet common framework defaults still conflate tool exposure with authorization. We audit whether LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex, and the Stripe Agent Toolkit re-authorize each model-emitted call, with concrete argument values, before execution. Across pinned public-source commits, all three provide capability gating by default, but none provides a deterministic fail-closed per-call value authorization gate by default. We introduce ScopeGate, a five-stage PDP/PEP for agent tool calls: scope, authorization, money ceiling, idempotency, and default deny. Evaluation shows the identical unauthorized payout call executes under LangChain's default dispatch (with a companion LlamaIndex PoC) but is denied by ScopeGate; the tested control reports 0/48 static bypasses, 0/29 unauthorized attempts (40-iteration adaptive run), 0/10 benign false-denies, and Latam-GPT payment-agent containment at 10/10. ASR denotes attempted unauthorized action, containment is not a cure, deployment-tier claims are inference over measured model classes, and no CVE is asserted.
tldr: This paper identifies authorization vulnerabilities in LLM agent frameworks where tool exposure is conflated with authorization, and proposes a five-stage gate to prevent confused-deputy attacks.
motivation: LLM agents with side-effecting tools (e.g., payments, email) are vulnerable to confused-deputy attacks when reading untrusted content, as current frameworks do not re-authorize each tool call.
method: The authors audit LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Stripe Agent Toolkit for per-call value authorization, and introduce ScopeGate, a five-stage PDP/PEP architecture (scope, authorization, money ceiling, idempotency, default deny).
result: All three frameworks provide capability gating but no deterministic fail-closed per-call authorization by default. ScopeGate blocks unauthorized payout calls that execute under default dispatches, with 0/48 static bypasses and 0/29 unauthorized attempts.
conclusion: Capability gating is insufficient; explicit per-call authorization is necessary to prevent confused-deputy failures in LLM agent frameworks.

title: Llm Semantic Signaling Game And Mechanism Design: Systematic Blindness, Awareness Shaping, And Mindset Dynamics
authors: Quanyan Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate strategic interactions through natural language, making semantic control a critical element of communication and deception. This paper develops a semantic signaling game in which a sender selects a semantic control, an LLM generates a stochastic message, and a receiver evaluates the message using an awareness-dependent scoring mechanism. Receiver awareness is modeled as a type that determines which linguistic features are perceived and used for inference, providing a formal model of systematic blindness. The framework connects prompt-based control, statistical detection, and game-theoretic equilibrium analysis. Gaussian approximations of aggregate message scores enable likelihood-ratio decision rules, while Perfect Bayesian Nash equilibria characterize strategic behavior. The paper further develops mechanism-design approaches that reshape receiver awareness, penalize deceptive semantic controls, and modify receiver populations to induce benign pooling equilibria. Numerical experiments validate the Gaussian approximation, quantify awareness-ordering effects, analyze mindset dynamics under adaptive adversaries, and demonstrate how awareness shaping and guardrail costs reduce successful phishing attacks. The proposed framework provides a principled foundation for analyzing strategic language-mediated interactions in agentic AI systems and offers new tools for the design of robust and secure human-AI communication.
tldr: This paper develops a semantic signaling game for LLM-mediated strategic interactions, focusing on deception and awareness shaping.
motivation: To model and analyze strategic communication and deception in LLM-mediated interactions, where receiver awareness is limited.
method: Formalizes a semantic signaling game with sender, LLM, and receiver; uses Gaussian approximations and Perfect Bayesian Nash equilibria.
result: Numerical experiments validate the Gaussian approximation and show that awareness shaping and guardrail costs reduce phishing attacks.
conclusion: The framework provides a foundation for analyzing strategic language-mediated interactions in agentic AI systems.

title: Syntactic Separation Implies Computational Indistinguishability: An Abstract Obstruction Theorem
authors: Fabio F. G. Buono
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that syntactic separation implies computational indistinguishability. A local syntactic system R acts on terms within radius r0 without consulting any model; when two Skolem functions are syntactically separated in R, no derivation can prove their equivalence (Case 1), and any sound local extension requires Omega(n) steps, improving to Omega(2^n) under clause-per-configuration encoding (Case 2). Both bounds are new: the derivation-length lower bound does not appear in prior work on Skolemization or saturation proving, and the cryptographic reading, syntactic separation as ciphertext indistinguishability, derivation cost as negligible advantage, is original. The same obstruction, as formal instances of Case 1 and Case 2, governs the Natural Proofs barrier of Razborov and Rudich, the Type Omitting Theorem, and the unconditional AC^0 barrier of Loff et al. (2026).
tldr: The paper proves that syntactic separation in a local syntactic system implies computational indistinguishability, with applications to proof complexity and the Natural Proofs barrier.
motivation: To establish a formal connection between syntactic separation in proof systems and computational indistinguishability, and to derive new lower bounds on derivation length.
method: The paper defines a local syntactic system R acting on terms within a radius r0, and shows that if two Skolem functions are syntactically separated in R, then no derivation can prove their equivalence, leading to lower bounds on derivation length.
result: New lower bounds on derivation length: Omega(n) steps in general, and Omega(2^n) under clause-per-configuration encoding. The paper also interprets syntactic separation as ciphertext indistinguishability and derivation cost as negligible advantage.
conclusion: Syntactic separation implies computational indistinguishability, and the same obstruction governs the Natural Proofs barrier, the Type Omitting Theorem, and the unconditional AC^0 barrier.

title: State-Evolution-based Score Matching For Generalized Approximate Message Passing
authors: Tomoharu Furudoi, Takumi Takahashi, Hideki Ochiai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalized approximate message passing (GAMP) equipped with minimum mean-square error (MMSE) denoisers, commonly referred to as Bayes-GAMP, is a powerful framework for solving inverse problems described by generalized linear models (GLMs) with arbitrary component-wise nonlinearities in the observation process. However, despite its theoretical tractability and rigorously established asymptotic optimality, the range of practical observation models for which Bayes-GAMP admits a closed-form implementation remains severely limited, particularly in complex-valued settings. This limitation largely stems from the restrictive requirement that the corresponding output denoiser, given by a conditional expectation, admit a closed-form expression. To overcome this limitation, we propose a principled approach that enables the implementation of Bayes-GAMP for complex-valued models with nonlinear observation mappings. Specifically, within a score-matching framework, we train a neural network to emulate the output denoiser using training data generated from a characterization of the message dynamics based on state evolution (SE). Notably, the proposed approach requires neither explicit evaluation of the denoiser nor knowledge of an explicit functional form of the nonlinear mapping; it requires only access to forward evaluations of the mapping during offline training. We show that, under ideal training conditions, GAMP with the trained network replacing the analytically intractable denoiser asymptotically matches the performance of Bayes-GAMP with the exact denoiser.
tldr: This paper proposes a neural network-based score matching method to implement Bayes-GAMP for complex-valued generalized linear models with intractable denoisers.
motivation: Bayes-GAMP is limited to observation models with closed-form denoisers, excluding many complex-valued nonlinear models. The authors aim to extend GAMP to such models without requiring explicit denoiser expressions.
method: They train a neural network to approximate the MMSE output denoiser using score matching, with training data generated from state evolution dynamics that characterize message passing.
result: Under ideal training, GAMP with the learned denoiser asymptotically matches the performance of Bayes-GAMP with the exact denoiser.
conclusion: The approach enables Bayes-GAMP for complex-valued nonlinear models, broadening its applicability to inverse problems where closed-form denoisers are unavailable.

title: Proportional-Fair Joint User Grouping And Power Allocation For Uplink Noma-isac
authors: Yaxuan Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This letter addresses long-term fairness in uplink non-orthogonal multiple access integrated sensing and communication (NOMA-ISAC) systems. Existing resource allocation schemes that maximize instantaneous sum rate often favor strong users, leaving historically underserved users with poor long-term throughput. We propose PF-JUGPA, a proportional-fair scheduling based joint user grouping and power allocation method. PF-JUGPA first pre-selects users via a PF metric combining instantaneous rate proxies and historical averages, then performs fairness-aware grouping and power allocation by maximizing a weighted sum rate whose weights are inversely proportional to historical service rates. Simulation results show that PF-JUGPA significantly improves the Jain fairness index and weak-user average rates with only a modest sum-rate loss compared to sum-rate-oriented and round-robin baselines. The findings confirm that embedding long-term service history into both scheduling and resource allocation yields an effective throughput--fairness--sensing tradeoff in uplink NOMA-ISAC.
tldr: This paper proposes a proportional-fair scheduling method for joint user grouping and power allocation in uplink NOMA-ISAC systems to improve long-term fairness.
motivation: Existing resource allocation schemes in NOMA-ISAC systems prioritize strong users, leading to poor long-term throughput for weak users. The paper aims to achieve a better trade-off between throughput, fairness, and sensing.
method: The proposed PF-JUGPA method pre-selects users using a proportional-fair metric that combines instantaneous rate proxies and historical averages, then performs fairness-aware grouping and power allocation by maximizing a weighted sum rate with weights inversely proportional to historical service rates.
result: Simulations show that PF-JUGPA significantly improves the Jain fairness index and weak-user average rates with only a modest sum-rate loss compared to sum-rate-oriented and round-robin baselines.
conclusion: Embedding long-term service history into both scheduling and resource allocation yields an effective throughput-fairness-sensing tradeoff in uplink NOMA-ISAC.

title: Exploring The Cryptographic Limits Of Transformer Networks
authors: Stefan Domunco, Andis Draguns, Philip Torr, Isaac Robinson, Christian Schroeder de Witt
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent work it has been shown that colluding AI agents can use steganographic methods to exchange malicious information. Whether a transformer can implement steganographic methods depends on what cryptographic functions it can implement, since a transformer that can implement a cryptographic function within its layers has source-free randomness access. Despite existing circuit-complexity results, no prior work maps specific cryptographic constructions to transformer architectures. As Merrill et al. have shown that saturated transformers can be seen as threshold circuits, we first generate threshold circuits for three different cryptographic constructions (Keccak functions, Merkle--Damgard constructions and Merkle Trees) and then map these circuits to different transformer architectures. We derive verified scaling laws for the width and depth of the circuits which implement each cryptographic construction and propose two different mappings: no-attention mapping, tokens-as-gates mapping. Beyond its security implications, this work contributes to by establishing a methodology for deriving structural guarantees on transformer computational capacity. Specifically, we derive constructive upper bounds on what a transformer of a given depth and width could plausibly compute, providing a principled foundation for capability evaluations of transformer-based AI systems.
tldr: This paper maps cryptographic constructions to transformer architectures using threshold circuits, deriving scaling laws for width and depth.
motivation: To understand whether transformers can implement steganographic methods by assessing their cryptographic capabilities.
method: The authors generate threshold circuits for Keccak, Merkle-Damgård, and Merkle Tree constructions, then map these circuits to transformer architectures using two mappings: no-attention and tokens-as-gates.
result: Verified scaling laws for the width and depth of circuits implementing each cryptographic construction, and derived constructive upper bounds on transformer computational capacity.
conclusion: The work provides a methodology for structural guarantees on transformer computational capacity, with implications for security and capability evaluations.

title: Robust Sparse Identification Of Nonlinear Dynamics Via Least Trimmed Squares
authors: Fabio Amaral, Geovani N. Grapiglia, Cassio M. Oishi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we propose a robust Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) pipeline for handling datasets corrupted by noise and outliers. The method decouples outlier filtering from sparse regression by combining Iterative Least Trimmed Squares (ILTS) with Sequentially Thresholded Least Squares (STLS). Unlike standard approaches that treat all observations uniformly within a single regression stage, the proposed ILTS-SINDy framework first applies an ILTS procedure that iteratively minimizes the sum of the smallest squared residuals to identify the most reliable observations without prior knowledge of outliers, after which STLS is used to recover a parsimonious governing model. Extensive numerical experiments show that ILTS-SINDy can significantly outperform existing robust SINDy variants across a range of outlier contamination levels, with performance maintained even under settings with up to [MATH] corrupted observations.
tldr: This paper proposes a robust method for identifying nonlinear dynamics from noisy data by combining iterative least trimmed squares with sparse regression.
motivation: Standard SINDy methods are sensitive to outliers, which can corrupt model identification. The authors aim to develop a pipeline that decouples outlier filtering from sparse regression to improve robustness.
method: The ILTS-SINDy framework first applies Iterative Least Trimmed Squares (ILTS) to iteratively minimize the sum of the smallest squared residuals, identifying reliable observations without prior knowledge of outliers. Then, Sequentially Thresholded Least Squares (STLS) is used to recover a parsimonious governing model.
result: Extensive numerical experiments show that ILTS-SINDy significantly outperforms existing robust SINDy variants across a range of outlier contamination levels, maintaining performance even with up to 50% corrupted observations.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a robust and effective approach for system identification in the presence of outliers, with potential applications in data-driven modeling of dynamical systems.

title: Convertible Codes: MSR-to-MSR Conversion With Optimal Access And Bandwidth
authors: Yumeng Yang, Han Cai, Xianfu Lei, Xiaohu Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study convertible codes in the merge regime and focus on the minimum storage regenerating (MSR) setting, where both the initial codes and the final code admit optimal single-node repair. We propose explicit MSR-to-MSR conversion schemes and analyze their performance in terms of access cost and conversion bandwidth. We first construct convertible MSR codes in the irregular setting, where the [MATH] initial codes may have different parameters, achieving optimal access cost. We further consider the practically important same-code setting, where all initial codewords are drawn from the same MSR code. By introducing a row-matching technique, we obtain constructions simultaneously achieving optimal access cost and conversion bandwidth in most parameter regimes.
tldr: This paper proposes explicit MSR-to-MSR conversion schemes for convertible codes in the merge regime, achieving optimal access cost and conversion bandwidth.
motivation: Convertible codes allow efficient code parameter changes in distributed storage systems, but existing work focuses on the merge regime for minimum storage regenerating (MSR) codes with optimal repair.
method: The authors construct convertible MSR codes in the irregular setting with optimal access cost, and introduce a row-matching technique for the same-code setting to simultaneously achieve optimal access and bandwidth.
result: The proposed constructions achieve optimal access cost in the irregular setting and optimal access and bandwidth in most parameter regimes for the same-code setting.
conclusion: This work provides efficient conversion schemes for MSR codes, advancing the theory of convertible codes for distributed storage.

title: Optimal Control Of Diffusive Mean-field Models For Swarming Particles On The Sphere
authors: Dohyun Kim Jinwook Jung
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a mean-field optimal control problem for a consensus (high-dimensional Kuramoto-type) dynamics with diffusion on the unit sphere. The control acts through a prescribed drift field and an interaction gain, and the cost functional is given to track a given target density while penalizing the control effort. At the microscopic level, we formulate the corresponding controlled [MATH]-particle Liouville problem and establish the existence of optimal controls. For fixed controls, we obtain a quantitative stochastic mean-field limit showing that the one-particle marginal converges to the mean-field solution with the convergence rate [MATH]. Finally, we show that microscopic optimal controls approximate a mean-field optimal control: any weak limit of particle-level minimizers is optimal for the mean-field problem.
tldr: This paper studies optimal control of diffusive mean-field models for swarming particles on a sphere, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to control consensus dynamics on the sphere, motivated by applications in swarming and collective behavior.
method: They formulate a mean-field optimal control problem for Kuramoto-type dynamics with diffusion, prove existence of optimal controls, and establish a quantitative stochastic mean-field limit.
result: They show that microscopic optimal controls approximate a mean-field optimal control, with convergence rate for the one-particle marginal.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for controlling swarming particles, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: A Theoretical Interpretation Of In-Context Learning Via Probabilistic Modeling
authors: Zhenyu Liu, Huaze Tang, Shao-Lun Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) is an emerging paradigm that employs the semantic information inherent in large language models (LLMs) for generating answers to user queries. While the remarkable performance of ICL has been widely known, a general modeling and a rigorous theoretical analysis of this paradigm are still lacking. This work presents a probabilistic model for ICL and derives the performance of ICL for both general parametric distributions and exponential families. Based on the derived results, the work explains the impact of multiple factors such as the number of demonstrations, the sensitivity of the probabilistic model to the variation of its parameters, as well as the similarity between the demonstrations and the query on the performance of ICL.
tldr: This paper proposes a probabilistic model for in-context learning in large language models and analyzes its performance theoretically.
motivation: In-context learning lacks a general theoretical framework; the authors aim to provide a rigorous probabilistic model to explain its behavior.
method: The authors develop a probabilistic model for ICL and derive performance bounds for general parametric distributions and exponential families.
result: The analysis explains how factors like number of demonstrations, parameter sensitivity, and demonstration-query similarity affect ICL performance.
conclusion: The probabilistic model offers a theoretical foundation for understanding ICL, but the work is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: An Information-Geometric Justification For Composite Coherence In Event-Based Narrative Extraction
authors: Brian Keith-Norambuena
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph-based narrative extraction relies on a coherence function to score transitions between events, but the coherence metrics in current use are defined operationally and lack an information-theoretic foundation. We study the composite metric [MATH], where [MATH] is the angular similarity of document embeddings and [MATH] is a topic proximity from the Jensen-Shannon distance of soft memberships, and give it an information-geometric reading together with an axiomatic characterization of the geometric-mean combinator. On the product manifold [MATH], the negative log-coherence decomposes additively into an angular and a topic cost. Because the Riemannian metric tensor induced by the Jensen-Shannon distance on the simplex is proportional to the Fisher information matrix, the topic component is locally consistent with the Fisher-Rao metric singled out by Chentsov's theorem. Within the compensability spectrum of combinators, the geometric mean is the unique one consistent with four natural axioms (a boundary/veto condition, symmetry, log-additivity, normalization), and the construction motivates a proper product metric [MATH]. Experiments on four corpora, three embedding families, and three topic models are consistent with the framework: the Fisher identity holds ([MATH]), the geometric mean tracks [MATH] closely ([MATH]), and a downstream LLM-as-judge check finds it is not dominated by any alternative combinator or single-channel baseline. Sweeping the spectrum, the bottleneck-coherence gap between extracted and random storylines splits into a symmetric component, maximized at the geometric mean across five corpora, and a displacement term; a cross-modal image-narrative case study reproduces the effect. These results justify the composite coherence metric and articulate when the geometric mean is the natural choice.
tldr: This paper provides an information-geometric justification for a composite coherence metric used in narrative extraction from text, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Current coherence metrics for graph-based narrative extraction lack an information-theoretic foundation. The authors aim to justify a composite metric combining angular similarity and topic proximity.
method: The paper analyzes the composite metric on a product manifold, showing that negative log-coherence decomposes additively. It uses the Fisher information matrix and Chentsov's theorem to argue for the geometric mean combinator, and validates with experiments on multiple corpora.
result: The geometric mean is the unique combinator satisfying four axioms, and experiments show it tracks the product metric closely. The bottleneck-coherence gap splits into symmetric and displacement components.
conclusion: The composite coherence metric is justified information-geometrically, and the geometric mean is the natural choice for combining angular and topic components.

title: Capacity Bounds And High-SNR Characterization For Mimo-owc Channels Under Average-Power Constraint
authors: Sufang Yang, Liang Xia, Longguang Li, Jintao Wang, Tao Jiang, Yuxin Wang, Ya Li, Hongjun He, Qixing Wang, Guangyi Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the capacity of multipleinput multiple-output (MIMO) optical wireless communication (OWC) channels under a total average-power constraint. Since different nonnegative input vectors can be mapped to the same image vector and thus induce the same output distribution, we formulate a nonnegative basis pursuit (NN-BP) problem to identify the minimum-l1-norm input vector for each image vector. Based on the NN-BP characterization, we derive an equivalent expression for the channel capacity in terms of the image-vector distribution. We then establish computable lower and upper capacity bounds for both nT >= nR and nT < nR cases, and prove that the proposed bounds are asymptotically tight in the high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime. Numerical results for indoor and outdoor OWC scenarios demonstrate that the proposed bounds improve upon existing ones and close the constant gap in the high-SNR regime.
tldr: This paper studies capacity bounds for MIMO optical wireless communication channels under average-power constraints, focusing on high-SNR characterization.
motivation: To derive tighter capacity bounds for MIMO-OWC channels that close the constant gap in the high-SNR regime, improving upon existing results.
method: Formulates a nonnegative basis pursuit problem to identify minimum-l1-norm input vectors, then derives equivalent capacity expression and computable lower/upper bounds.
result: Proposed bounds are asymptotically tight in high SNR and numerically outperform existing bounds for indoor and outdoor OWC scenarios.
conclusion: The work provides improved capacity characterization for MIMO-OWC channels, but is focused on classical optical communication without quantum information or thermodynamics aspects.

title: How To Untwist Twisted Gauge Fields
authors: Serge Lazzarini, Thierry Masson, Louis Usala
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper provides an isomorphism between the space of twisted gauge fields on a principal bundle [MATH] and the space of standard gauge fields on a different principal bundle [MATH] associated to [MATH]. This isomorphism extends to local fields on the base manifold, which enables the use of local twisted fields in standard gauge theories (e.g. Yang-Mills-like theories). This allows one to deal with two symmetry groups, coming from [MATH] and [MATH], respectively. The construction makes use of a larger principal bundle [MATH] which has [MATH] and [MATH] as quotient bundles. The gauge structure on [MATH] encodes both standard and twisted gauge structures on [MATH]. In addition, the isomorphism classes of bundles [MATH] are in 1:1 correspondence with the equivalence classes of cocycles (up to a coboundary). This paper also provides a new interpretation of (full) dressing fields as dynamic (or active) sections of a principal bundle.
tldr: This paper establishes an isomorphism between twisted and standard gauge fields on principal bundles, enabling the use of twisted fields in standard gauge theories.
motivation: To provide a rigorous mathematical framework for twisted gauge fields and relate them to standard gauge theories, facilitating their application in physics.
method: The authors construct a larger principal bundle that encodes both standard and twisted gauge structures, and prove an isomorphism between the spaces of twisted and standard gauge fields.
result: An isomorphism is established that extends to local fields, allowing twisted fields to be used in Yang-Mills-like theories, and a new interpretation of dressing fields is provided.
conclusion: The work offers a unified geometric perspective on twisted gauge fields and their relation to standard gauge theories, with potential applications in theoretical physics.

title: Matrix Representations Of Finite Fields
authors: Tzu-Wei Lin, Bo-Jiun Lee, Hsin-Po Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite fields are important algebraic structures that have a wide range of applications in fields such as coding theory and cryptography. But the standard construction of finite field extensions through polynomial quotients is computationally opaque, especially when we want to identify a degree-[MATH] extension of [MATH] and a degree-[MATH] extension of [MATH]. In this short note, we present a coherent family of representations by matrices [MATH] for all prime powers [MATH] and all degrees [MATH]. These maps are chosen so that concatenating [MATH] and [MATH] recovers [MATH] up to row and column permutations. As a consequence, the images of [MATH] can be partitioned into four [MATH] blocks or nine [MATH] blocks to visualize the subfield chains [MATH] and [MATH] at the same time. A variant [MATH] is also discussed, wherein the Frobenius automorphism is represented by a cyclic shift of rows and columns. From an educational point of view, these rhos give explicit and self-contained mental models of finite fields; subfields, trace, norm, minimal polynomial, and Frobenius all become visible through matrix algebra accessible to most students. From a theoretical point of view, the construction exhibits structural implications of Conway polynomials and the normal basis theorem.
tldr: This paper presents matrix representations of finite fields that make subfield chains and Frobenius automorphism explicit.
motivation: Standard polynomial quotient construction of finite field extensions is computationally opaque, especially for identifying subfield chains.
method: The authors construct a family of matrix representations for all prime powers and degrees, designed so that concatenating representations recovers the original up to permutations, and a variant where Frobenius is a cyclic shift.
result: The matrix representations visualize subfield chains, trace, norm, minimal polynomial, and Frobenius automorphism through matrix algebra.
conclusion: The construction provides explicit mental models for educational purposes and reveals structural implications of Conway polynomials and the normal basis theorem.

title: Exit-and-Join Dynamics And Equilibrium In Continuum Cooperative Games
authors: Quanyan Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a continuum theory of exit-and-join coalition dynamics in nonatomic cooperative games. We extend the Aumann-Shapley value and the Aumann-Dr\`eze value to coalition structures in which each coalition is treated as a restricted nonatomic game, yielding a marginal-contribution-based payoff density that governs incentives for agents to remain in, exit, or join coalitions. We derive deterministic mean-field dynamics from decentralized switching rules and show that payoff-difference switching recovers replicator dynamics as a special case. We characterize exit-and-join equilibrium by the absence of profitable positive-mass deviations and prove its equivalence with stationarity of the induced mass dynamics under incentive-compatible and strictly payoff-responsive switching rates. For mass-based cooperative games, we construct a Lyapunov function and establish global convergence under strict concavity. We further show that the equilibrium is equivalent to a Wardrop equilibrium of an induced nonatomic population game and admits a variational inequality formulation. The framework is extended to incorporate switching costs and endogenous coalition acceptance rules, leading to constrained equilibria characterized by quasi-variational inequalities. The proposed theory unifies cooperative value allocation, noncooperative coalition mobility, mean-field dynamics, evolutionary game theory, and population games within a common framework for analyzing coalition formation and adaptation in large-scale multi-agent systems.
tldr: This paper develops a continuum theory of coalition dynamics in nonatomic cooperative games, unifying cooperative value allocation, mean-field dynamics, and evolutionary game theory.
motivation: To understand how large-scale multi-agent systems form and adapt coalitions over time, bridging cooperative game theory and noncooperative dynamics.
method: Extends Aumann-Shapley and Aumann-Drèze values to coalition structures, derives deterministic mean-field dynamics from decentralized switching rules, and characterizes equilibrium via variational inequalities.
result: Establishes equivalence between exit-and-join equilibrium and stationarity of mass dynamics, proves global convergence for mass-based games, and extends to switching costs and endogenous acceptance rules.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified approach to coalition formation and adaptation in large-scale multi-agent systems, with connections to evolutionary game theory and population games.

title: Optically Dense Nanowire Metamaterials Are Transparent To Polarization
authors: Shravan Raghunathan, Ad Lagendijk, Willem L. Vos
abstract: ArXiv:2606.29019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the transport of light through dense opaque anisotropic metamaterials consisting of oriented nanowires. The nanowires consist of polymer photoresist that is structured by direct laser writing (DLW) with two-photon induced polymerization, with radii between [MATH] and [MATH]. Our flat samples have a thickness up to 9 layers, from [MATH] to [MATH]. Within each layer, the nanowires are parallel and spaced with random nearest-neighbor distances; nanowires in adjacent layers are perpendicular. The diffuse optical transmission at [MATH]nm is as low as [MATH], typical of optically dense, multiple scattering metamaterials, with a mean free path down to [MATH], much less than the sample thickness. It is striking that the linear polarization of the input light is maintained at the output of the dense nanowire samples, and not scrambled as in dense nanosphere arrays. Moreover, the linear output polarization faithfully tracks the input polarization. We propose that the polarization is maintained in our optically thick samples, since light is predominantly transported perpendicularly to the nanowire layers. The polarization vector then lies in the nanowire plane, consisting of a linear combination of parallel and perpendicular vectors that are both conserved upon subsequent scattering. Hence, the polarization remains independent of nanowire orientation, even after multiple scattering events. We propose that anisotropic scattering samples may find practical uses in white LEDs and its applications in lighting luminaires, optical communication, and encryption systems.
tldr: This paper studies light transport through dense nanowire metamaterials, finding that linear polarization is preserved despite multiple scattering.
motivation: Understanding polarization transport in dense anisotropic media is important for applications in lighting and optical communication.
method: The authors fabricate nanowire metamaterials using direct laser writing and measure diffuse optical transmission and output polarization.
result: Linear polarization is maintained and tracks the input polarization, unlike in dense nanosphere arrays, due to light transport perpendicular to nanowire layers.
conclusion: Anisotropic scattering samples can preserve polarization, suggesting practical uses in white LEDs, optical communication, and encryption.

title: Sequential Ordering Relations With Application To Fuzzy Numbers
authors: Garc\'ia-Zamora, Diego, Rold\'an L\'opez de Hierro, Antonio Francisco
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ranking of fuzzy numbers has become a challenging task in fuzzy set theory due to their complex, multi-dimensional nature. While the Klir-Yuan partial order provides a natural term-wise comparison of [MATH]-cuts, it often leaves many fuzzy numbers incomparable. To address this, various ranking methods have been developed to construct total preorders between them. However, many classical approaches suffer from significant information loss as they imply a defuzzification process. On the other hand, approaches such as admissible orders allow defining total orders, but at the expense of imposing strict algebraic rules that may contradict human intuition. In this study, we introduce a generalized sequential ordering framework to overcome these limitations. By establishing a sequence space over a totally preordered base space, we construct a flexible lexicographical structure that sequentially resolves ties. We prove that this framework yields total preorders and, under injectivity conditions, total orders. Furthermore, we analyze the compatibility of these sequential orders with the notion of admissibility. We also show that our proposed framework provides a unified mathematical umbrella that encompasses and generalizes existing ranking techniques, offering highly discriminative ordering relations for fuzzy numbers and beyond.
tldr: This paper introduces a sequential ordering framework for ranking fuzzy numbers, addressing incomparability issues in partial orders.
motivation: Existing ranking methods for fuzzy numbers either suffer from information loss or impose restrictive algebraic rules; a more flexible and general ordering framework is needed.
method: The authors define a sequence space over a totally preordered base space and construct a lexicographical structure that sequentially resolves ties, proving it yields total preorders and, under injectivity, total orders.
result: The framework generalizes existing ranking techniques and provides highly discriminative ordering relations for fuzzy numbers.
conclusion: The proposed sequential ordering framework offers a unified mathematical umbrella for ranking fuzzy numbers and can be extended to other domains.

title: Constrained Kolmogorov Widths
authors: Ronald Devore, Guergana Petrova, Jonathan W. Siegel, Przemys{\l}aw Wojtaszczyk
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main theme of approximation theory is to understand how well a general function [MATH] can be approximated by a simpler function [MATH] such as a polynomial or spline. In many applications, one wants [MATH] to retain known properties of [MATH] such as its inherent smoothness or a geometrical property such as monotonicity or convexity. Additional requirements on [MATH] of this type are known as constraints. In this paper, we do a systematic study of constrained approximation to understand how the imposition of such constraints limits the efficiency of the approximation. We study constrained approximation in the setting of linear approximation where [MATH] is to be taken from a finite dimensional linear space [MATH] of a fixed dimension [MATH]. Kolmogorov widths describe how well one can approximate when using such linear spaces [MATH]. The first part of this paper introduces and studies several types of constrained widths, including the constrained Kolmogorov widths, and gives comparisons between them. The second part of the paper is restricted to classical settings where the constraint imposes a smoothness requirement on [MATH]. In this case, our results prove that the additional constraint can typically be imposed with no loss in the efficiency of the approximation.
tldr: This paper studies constrained approximation in linear approximation theory, introducing constrained Kolmogorov widths and showing that smoothness constraints can often be imposed without loss of efficiency.
motivation: In many applications, approximations must preserve properties like smoothness or convexity, but the impact of such constraints on approximation efficiency is not well understood.
method: The authors define several types of constrained widths, compare them, and analyze the case where the constraint is a smoothness requirement using classical approximation theory tools.
result: They prove that in classical settings, imposing a smoothness constraint typically does not reduce the efficiency of the approximation.
conclusion: Constrained approximation can be as efficient as unconstrained approximation when the constraint is a smoothness condition, which is beneficial for practical applications.

title: Lipschitz Regularity In Wasserstein Robust Stochastic Optimal Control
authors: Jose Blanchet Shengbo Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robust Markov decision processes provide a principled framework for protecting sequential decision-making against transition-law misspecification and have attracted substantial recent research interest. As in non-robust stochastic optimal control, an important question is whether the robust value function is sufficiently regular for approximation and learning. This paper studies Lipschitz regularity of optimal value functions for Wasserstein robust stochastic optimal control on possibly unbounded Polish state spaces under an infinite-horizon discounted reward criterion. We consider two robustness formulations: a kernel-robust model, in which the adversary perturbs the next-state distribution within a Wasserstein ball around a nominal transition kernel, and a noise-robust model, in which the adversary perturbs the driving noise of the state transition dynamics. In the non-robust setting, Lipschitz rewards and Lipschitz transition dynamics do not, in general, imply a Lipschitz value function. In contrast, we show that in these Wasserstein robust formulations, Lipschitz assumptions on the model primitives yield Lipschitz robust value functions. Thus, Wasserstein robustness not only protects against misspecification but also regularizes the Bellman fixed point, providing stability relevant to discretization, value-function approximation, estimation, and learning.
tldr: This paper studies Lipschitz regularity of value functions in Wasserstein robust stochastic optimal control, a topic in robust control theory.
motivation: Robust Markov decision processes protect against transition model misspecification, but the regularity of value functions is crucial for approximation and learning.
method: The authors analyze two robustness formulations (kernel-robust and noise-robust) and prove that Lipschitz assumptions on model primitives yield Lipschitz robust value functions.
result: Unlike non-robust settings, Wasserstein robustness regularizes the Bellman fixed point, ensuring Lipschitz continuity of the optimal value function.
conclusion: Wasserstein robustness not only guards against misspecification but also provides stability beneficial for discretization, approximation, and learning.

title: Dimensional Entropy Of Amenable Group Actions Over Stable Sets And Fibres
authors: Guohua Zhang Xinyao He
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of Bowen's dimensional entropy on subsets for actions of amenable groups. We prove three main results. (1) First, topological conditional entropy is characterized by the dimensional entropy of stable sets (Theorem 1.1), answering a question of Dou, Wang and the second author of the present paper raised in [Fund. Math., 2025]. We remark that our Theorem 1.1 is the first characterization of topological conditional entropy via Bowen's dimensional entropy of stable sets even for [MATH]-actions. (2) Second, we establish a dimensional entropy inequality for factor maps (Theorem 1.2). It relates dimensional entropy of a set to that of its image and topological entropy of fibres, and may be viewed as the dimensional-entropy counterpart of the factor-map inequality for packing topological entropy due to Dou, Zheng, and Zhou proved as Theorem 1.4 in [Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems, 2023]. (3) Third, the relative topological entropy of a factor map is determined by the dimensional entropy of the fibres (Theorem 1.3). Notably, our proof of this formula (Theorem 1.3) is purely topological, in contrast to the recent measure-theoretic approach of Dou, Wang and Zhou based on relative Shannon--McMillan--Breiman theorems.
